nodes.name: Ni-MOF precursor preparation
nodes.procedure: Ni-BDC precursor was prepared as reported previously [13] and characterized using SEM and TEM. The Ni-BDC MOF is composed of ultrathin nanosheets with an average vertical height of ≈10 μm. These nanosheets are vertically grown on the acid-treated nickel foam (NF).
nodes.source_text: Prior to the MOF derivatization, as-prepared Ni-BDC precursor[13] was characterized using scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and transmission electron microscopy (TEM).

nodes.name: Electrochemical MOF derivation to V_Ni-Ni(OH)_x
nodes.procedure: Ni-BDC nanosheets vertically grown on acid-treated nickel foam undergo alkali etching with electric field assistance via cyclic voltammetry (CV) in alkaline electrolyte. BDC organic ligand is gradually removed. After exposure to metal ions and OH⁻ ions, hydroxide forms in situ. Derivation completes after 400 CV cycles, yielding thicker, rougher V_Ni-Ni(OH)_x nanosheets with Ni²⁺ vacancies.

unit_operations.name: Cyclic Voltammetry
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: The derivation of XRD patterns is stopped after 400 CV cycles.

unit_operations.name: Alkali Etching
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: With the help of alkali etching and the driving force of an electric field, the BDC organic ligand is gradually removed from these nanosheets.

nodes.name: Pt single atom incorporation during MOF derivation
nodes.procedure: During the electrochemical reduction process of Ni-MOF in 1 M KOH solution, platinum source is added. Ni²⁺ vacancies in the forming Ni(OH)_x serve as trapping sites to capture reduced Pt single atoms, which form Pt-O₄ tetradentate coordination structure, yielding Pt-Ni(OH)_x with 0.17 wt% Pt loading.
nodes.source_text: Once a platinum source is added into 1M KOH solution during this electrochemical reduction process, the Ni²⁺ vacancies are possible to serve as a hole to capture the reduced Pt single atoms

nodes.name: Ir single atom seeding on V_Ni-Ni(OH)_x
nodes.procedure: Ir single atoms have been loaded on V_Ni-Ni(OH)_x support by use of the same preparation process as Pt-Ni(OH)_x to form Ir-Ni(OH)_x.
nodes.source_text: this sowing strategy can be employed to synthesize other NMSACs, for example, those from Ir and Ru. Their single atoms have been loaded on V_Ni - Ni(OH)_x support by use of the same preparation process.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt-Ni(OH)x inherits the curly nanosheet morphology of V_Ni-Ni(OH)x.
nodes.evidence_snippet: SEM image of this Pt based catalyst (Figure 2a) was recorded and compared with that of V_{Ni} - Ni(OH)_x . The Pt - Ni(OH)_x inherits the morphology of the V_{Ni} - Ni(OH)_x curly nanosheets.

nodes.characterization_summary: High-resolution TEM shows lattice fringes of 0.23 nm and 0.27 nm corresponding to (011) and (100) planes of Ni(OH)2 phase with no Pt nanoparticles.
nodes.evidence_snippet: From its high-resolution TEM image (Figure S5, Supporting Information), its crystal structure is revealed, where no emerged Pt nanoparticles are seen.

nodes.characterization_summary: Aberration-corrected HAADF-STEM shows all Pt species exist at isolated single atomic sites exclusively, neither clusters nor nanoparticles detected.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the aberration-corrected high-angle annular dark-field STEM (HAADF-STEM) analysis (Figure 2b and Figure S6, Supporting Information) of this Pt - Ni(OH)_x catalyst was performed to disclose the existing state of platinum species inside this catalyst.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS elemental mapping confirms uniform distribution of Ni, O, and Pt elements.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The energy dispersive spectroscopy (EDS) elemental mapping (Figure 2c) further confirms the existence of Pt species as well as the uniform distribution of Ni, O, and Pt elements.

nodes.characterization_summary: All peaks assigned to β-Ni(OH)2 phase (PDF#73-1520) due to ultralow Pt intake.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the XRD patterns of the Pt - Ni(OH)_x catalyst (Figure 2d), all peaks are assigned to the β-Ni(OH)_2 phase (PDF#73-1520), due to ultralow intake of platinum.
The amount of Pt in the Pt - Ni(OH)_x catalyst, calculated by means of inductively coupled plasma-mass spectrometry (ICP-MS), is only about 0.17wt% .

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt 4f XPS shows peaks at 69.3 eV (Pt 4f7/2) and 72.6 eV (Pt 4f5/2) with 3.3 eV spin-energy separation. Ni 2p shows Ni2+ (855.0/872.8 eV), Ni3+ (856.4/874.2 eV from defects), and satellites (861.0/879.2 eV). Ni3+ content reduced from 22.72 at% to 15.66 at% after Pt incorporation with 0.8 eV positive shift.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In its Pt 4f XPS spectrum (Figure 2e), the deconvoluted peaks are located at 69.3 and 72.6eV... Note that the content of Ni3+ species in V_{Ni} - Ni(OH)_2 was reduced from 22.72 at% to 15.66 at% after the incorporation of Pt (Tables S1 and S2, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni K-edge: highest white line intensity for V_Ni-Ni(OH)x due to cation vacancies, reduced after Pt incorporation indicating lower Ni valence. Pre-edge peak at ~8333 eV from distorted Ni-O6 geometry. Pt L3-edge: calculated average Pt valence +1.52.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the XANES Ni K-edge spectra (Figure 3a), ... The calculated average valence state of a Pt atom in the Pt - N_i(OH)_x catalyst is +1.52...

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni K-edge FT-EXAFS: Ni-O at 1.5 Å, Ni-Ni at 2.7 Å; shortest Ni-Ni distance in V_Ni-Ni(OH)x indicates coordinatively unsaturated sites. Pt L3-edge: Pt-O at 1.5 Å (CN=3.4), no Pt-Pt contribution confirming atomic dispersion and Pt-O4 coordination.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Ni K-edge FT-EXAFS spectrum of the Pt - N_i(OH)_x catalyst exhibits a significant difference... The estimated coordination number (CN) of the first Pt-O shell using EXAFS fitting at the Pt - N_i(OH)_x catalyst... is 3.4.

nodes.characterization_summary: Double-layer capacitance C_dl = 4.3 μF cm^-2, 5 times higher than V_Ni-Ni(OH)x.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The C_dl value of the Pt - Ni(OH)_x catalyst is 4.3 μF cm^{-2} (Figure 4d), 5 times higher than that (0.7 μF cm^{-2}) of the V_{Ni} - Ni(OH)_x catalyst.

nodes.characterization_summary: Smallest semicircle diameter indicates lowest charge transfer resistance R_ct.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The smallest diameter of the semicircle in the Nyquist plot of the Pt - Ni(OH)_x catalyst indicates its lowest charge transfer resistance (R_ct).

nodes.characterization_summary: V_Ni-Ni(OH)x shows strongest Ni2+ vacancy emission at 510 nm; intensity decreases more significantly than O vacancy (400 nm) after Pt incorporation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The photoluminescence (PL) emission spectra of Ni2+ vacancies (Figure S4, Supporting Information) were thus recorded... Compared to Ni(OH)2 and Pt - N_i(OH)_x electrocatalyst, the V_{Ni} - Ni(OH)_x catalyst shows the strongest intensity of Ni2+ vacancies.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni surface content 12 at% vs bulk 27 at%; Pt surface content 1.08 at% decreasing with etching depth, confirming surficial Ni2+ vacancies trapping Pt.
nodes.evidence_snippet: To investigate the distribution states of Pt and Ni elements, XPS depth profiling was conducted on the Pt - Ni(OH)_x nanosheets (Figure S10, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: Bandgap reduced from 4.12-4.13 eV (V_Ni-Ni(OH)x, β-Ni(OH)2) to 4.05 eV after Pt incorporation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the bandgap value (4.05eV) of the β-Ni(OH)2 catalyst. This probably results from the aggregation of local electrons...
